Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1a) demonstrates a dense consolidation in the right upper lobe that is sharply demarcated inferiorly by the horizontal fissure, indicating it respects anatomical boundaries. This pattern, often accompanied by air bronchograms (visible air-filled bronchi within the opacity), is the classic radiographic presentation of lobar pneumonia caused by an infectious process.
